name: Lumen
description: Plays files as they are: the browser remuxes them and decodes the audio, the server only sends bytes. Measured against the regular player, on files the server would otherwise repackage or transcode: playback starts 2 to 4 times sooner, seeks are 3 to 4 times faster, and changing the audio track is about 8 times faster.
overview: Playback without server-side transcoding for the web client.

versions.changelog: The journal records how playback starts after the first frame of each opening: player events and seconds buffered ahead.
The picture stays hidden until the resume position is on screen: a frame from another shot could flash when resuming or changing the audio track. The journal records the first frames of each opening.

Faster start and resume: the file is checked while the web client negotiates and prepared from its detail page. Audio track changes no longer go back to the server. Fixes the position lost after a network drop when the journal is off.
The plugin page shows the measured gains: start, seeks and audio track changes.
The messages Lumen writes to the browser console are now in English.
The playback log tells apart, in the opening of a playback, the time spent negotiating with the server and the time the web client takes to create its video element.
When its source is lost (a failure during playback, or the page coming back from the background), Lumen reopens the film at the same position before handing over to the regular player.
On TVs and game consoles, playback stays with the regular player. Two quick skips in a row now add up while a seek is in progress.
Seeking inside what is already loaded no longer reloads it. The playback log records where the opening time goes.
iPhone and iPad: sound now plays when the device is in silent mode, as in any video app.
With "Play with Lumen" unchecked, files the server direct-plays are no longer played by Lumen. The first logged playback now appears in the log.
Maintenance release: code comments cleaned up, no change in behaviour.
